info.title: DalTime API
info.description:
Generated from the Zod schemas in `contracts/src/schemas`. Do not edit by hand — run `npm run generate` in `contracts/` instead.

Beyond the standard OpenAPI fields, every operation carries two vendor extensions:
- `x-implementation-path`: the repo-relative files implementing it.
- `x-dynamodb-access`: the real DynamoDB commands and key conditions it issues, so the full set of access patterns can be read from this file alone.

get.summary: List shifts other employees have offered up for pickup on a date
get.description: Backs the "Available to Take" panel (frontend/src/app/features/employee/available-shifts) — shifts from OTHER employees in the caller’s org that are published and flagged available_for_pickup for the requested date. An employee can never pick up their own shift.

x-dynamodb-access.note: Resolves the caller’s org_id and employee_id; a missing record fails closed with 403.

x-dynamodb-access.filter: #date = :date AND available_for_pickup = :true AND employee_id <> :callerId AND (#status = :published OR attribute_not_exists(#status))
x-dynamodb-access.note: Base-table query narrowed to the org partition. The filter excludes the caller’s own shifts, requires the assigned employee to have opted the shift into pickup, and requires published status.

get.summary: List the calling employee’s own shifts within a time window
get.description: Backs the employee shifts calendar (frontend/src/app/features/employee/shifts), scoped to exactly one of a month, a single day, or a 7-day week starting on a given date.

x-dynamodb-access.note: Resolves the caller’s org_id and employee_id; a missing record fails closed with 403.

x-dynamodb-access.filter: employee_id = :employeeId AND begins_with(#date, :month) AND (#status = :published OR attribute_not_exists(#status))
x-dynamodb-access.note: Variant used when ?month=YYYY-MM is supplied.
Variant used when ?date=YYYY-MM-DD is supplied.

x-dynamodb-access.filter: employee_id = :employeeId AND #date >= :weekStart AND #date <= :weekEnd AND (#status = :published OR attribute_not_exists(#status))
x-dynamodb-access.note: Variant used when ?week=YYYY-MM-DD is supplied. weekEnd = weekStart + 6 days; YYYY-MM-DD lexicographic order matches chronological order so no GSI is needed.

post.summary: Post one of the caller’s own published shifts for swap
post.description: Lets an employee offer a shift they no longer want for a coworker to claim. Notifies the shift’s manager (best-effort) once the listing is created.

x-dynamodb-access.note: Resolves the caller’s org_id, employee_id, and display name; a missing record fails closed with 403.
Validates the shift exists, belongs to the caller, is published, and is not in the past.
Duplicate-post guard — rejects with 409 if the caller already has an open listing for this shift.
Reads the caller’s manager_id (not present on the METADATA reverse-lookup) to denormalize onto the listing.
Creates the listing with GSI1SK = STATUS#open#<created_at>.
Best-effort manager notification; a write failure here does not fail the request.

post.description: Transfers an open listing’s shift to the claiming employee. Notifies the shift’s manager (best-effort) once the transfer succeeds.

x-dynamodb-access.note: Resolves the caller’s org_id, employee_id, and display name; a missing record fails closed with 403.
Org-scoped, so a cross-org swapId returns null (404, not 403) — avoids leaking listing existence across orgs. Also rejects self-claim and non-open status.
Marks the listing claimed and flips GSI1SK to STATUS#claimed#<created_at>. The condition makes the claim atomic: a losing concurrent claimer gets ConditionalCheckFailedException, mapped to 409.
Transfers the shift’s employee_id/employee_name to the claimer. Run in parallel with the SWAP# update.

get.description: Public smoke-test target with no auth requirement, hit by CI/CD post-deploy checks (frontend/src/environments + deploy workflows) to confirm the HttpApi route and Lambda runtime are alive after a deployment. The handler wraps its body in a try/catch that always returns a shaped 200, even on an internal error, so the heartbeat itself never reports a false negative.

Backs the notification bell and notification list page (frontend/src/app/shared/notifications) for the web-admin role. One Lambda (`NotificationsFunction`) serves this identically across all four role prefixes — the prefix only scopes which JWT-authenticated role may call it, not the behaviour, which is always "list the caller's own notifications by their JWT sub".

x-dynamodb-access.note: ScanIndexForward: false. SK embeds `created_at` first, so newest-first ordering falls out of the base-table sort key with no GSI required.

patch.summary: Mark all of the calling web-admin's unread notifications as read
patch.description: Backs the notification list page’s "mark all as read" action. Distinct from the `{notificationId}` variant below: this route takes no path parameter and no request body — it marks every one of the caller’s currently-unread notifications and returns only a count, never the notifications themselves.

x-dynamodb-access.note: ScanIndexForward: false. Finds only the caller’s currently-unread notifications.

x-dynamodb-access.keyCondition: PK = USER#<callerSub> AND SK = <SK of each item returned by the Query above>
x-dynamodb-access.note: One UpdateItem per unread item found above, issued in parallel via `Promise.all` — sets `read = true`. Skipped entirely (no writes) when the caller has zero unread notifications.

200.description: How many notifications were marked read.

patch.summary: Mark one of the calling web-admin's notifications as read
patch.description: Backs marking a single notification as read from the notification bell/list — e.g. clicking an individual unread item. Distinct from the no-id variant above: this route addresses exactly one notification by its `notificationId` path parameter and returns that notification (now read), not a count. An empty-string `notificationId` (present-but-blank path param) is rejected with 400 before the service is called, rather than silently falling through to mark-all semantics.

x-dynamodb-access.note: Scoped to the caller’s own partition — a forged/foreign notificationId simply yields no item, so the service throws NotFoundError (404), never ForbiddenError, avoiding existence leakage. This Get is also how ownership is verified; there is no separate authorization check.
Only issued if the Get above found an item that was not already read — sets `read = true`. Skipped (item returned as-is) when the notification was already read.

schema.description: Opaque composite id `<created_at>#<rawId>` returned as `notification_id` on list/create. Must be `encodeURIComponent`-encoded by the caller.
